title: Lifecycle validation report
description: One harness run against one support row. Written by tools/validation/lifecycle-stages.sh and consumed by evidence-bundle assembly, which decides completeness from the stage set rather than from prose.

log.description: The sub-case's log, relative to the report. Attached whether it ran or not.

detail.description: Why the sub-case failed or was skipped. Required for both.

row_id.description: The support row this run validates. A report whose row is not in the registry is evidence for nothing.

subject.description: What was actually installed and exercised. A report that does not say what it tested cannot authorize a release: without it a run filed under one version silently blesses every later tag.

tested_version.description: The release version this run authorizes, as the release workflow resolves it (`meta.outputs.version`) -- always bare X.Y.Z, including when the artifacts under test came from a candidate. NOT the package version string: a candidate's .deb reports 0.2.1~rc.1 and its wheel 0.2.1rc1, and recording either here would be recording which build was installed rather than which release the evidence stands for. That fact belongs in artifact_digest. The `~` form is deliberately outside the pattern so it cannot be filed here by accident.

source_revision.description: Full git SHA of the source the tested artifacts were built from, when the harness can determine it.

artifact_digest.description: sha256 of the one immutable artifact the install verified, recorded by the harness while the run was happening. Binds the report to specific bytes rather than to a version string anyone can reuse. Which artifact that is depends on how the row installs: for a package channel it is the release's signed SHA256SUMS, which commits transitively to every package installed; for a build-from-source channel it is the archive every formula is pinned to, which is that channel's only immutable artifact -- and therefore names the build input, not the bytes that landed. The harness records what it hashed in `artifact-digest.txt` beside the stage logs, since this object is closed and cannot carry it. Bare lowercase hex: the `sha256:`-prefixed spelling used for model artifacts is deliberately outside the pattern so the two cannot be confused. Optional, because a report is worth filing from a harness that cannot determine it -- but a value not captured during the run cannot be recovered afterwards, since nothing on an installed system reports which artifact it came from.

harness.description: Which harness produced this run, for reproducing it.

outcome.description: pass only when all eight canonical stages are present and passed and, if the report carries the reboot stage, it passed too. fail when any stage failed, the reboot stage included. incomplete when nothing failed but the eight are not all present and passing -- a deliberate skip is not a breakage, and conflating the two would either hide a gap or invent a failure. Only pass satisfies the release gate.

reboot.description: The reboot stage: a stage beside the canonical eight, not one of them, because only some rows at some versions run it and every other report must stay exactly as it is. It crosses a host reboot (the runner persists the run across it) and asserts, in this order because each consumes the state the one before leaves, that with the machine's cloud metadata blocked the agent fails closed after its retry window (blocked), that lifting the block inside the window recovers the committed set with no reprovisioning (transient), and that denied-egress operation then resumes within the new boot (denied_egress_resumes). Absent from a report, it was not run; the release gate decides which rows and versions require it.

status.description: pass only when the boot ID changed, all three sub-cases passed and the retry window was recorded. There is no skipped: a reboot stage that did not run is absent, never present and skipped.

log.description: The stage's log, relative to the report.

detail.description: Why the stage failed. Required when it did.

boot_id_changed.description: Whether the kernel boot ID after the reboot differs from the one recorded before it. false means no reboot happened, whatever else passed.

retry_window_seconds.description: The agent's metadata retry window as the run observed it, in seconds. Absent when the run never reached a point where it could be observed, and then the stage failed.

sub_cases.description: The three sub-cases, each present whether it ran or not, so a report cannot quietly leave one out.

stage.description: The eight lifecycle stages. A closed set so a report missing one is detectable rather than merely shorter.

started_at.description: When the stage began. Present only for a stage that ran.

finished_at.description: When the stage ended. Present only for a stage that ran.

log.description: Log file for this stage, relative to the report. Attached whether the stage passed or failed: a passing stage's log is what a later regression is diffed against.

detail.description: Why a stage failed or was skipped. Required for both, since an unexplained skip is indistinguishable from an omission.
